description: A build-a-circuit assignment: make a 10 V source and a 10 Mohm voltmeter read 2.5 V with exactly two resistors. The starting circuit holds the locked source V1 (ideal, 10 V), the locked voltmeter VM1 (10 Mohm) wired from the output node to ground, and a ground marker; the student adds the resistors. The values come from the divider equation with the meter's 10 Mohm in parallel with the bottom resistor, not from Engine output.

attempts.name: correct
attempts.description: R_top 30 kOhm from V1+ to the output node, R_bottom 10 kOhm from the output node to ground.

attempts.name: three-resistors
attempts.description: The top resistor is 20 kOhm in series with 10 kOhm and the bottom one is 10 kOhm: the same 2.498126405 V, but three resistors.

attempts.name: equal-resistors
attempts.description: R_top and R_bottom both 10 kOhm: two resistors, wrong ratio.

attempts.name: no-resistors
attempts.description: Nothing added: the output node is held at ground by the voltmeter alone, so it reads 0 V.

attempts.name: locked-part-changed
attempts.description: The correct 30 kOhm and 10 kOhm resistors, but the locked source was set to 20 V in a modified file or editor. The reading is no longer right and the integrity check reports the change.

expected.note: A failed integrity check makes the outcome failed whatever the other criteria say.

attempts.name: source-shorted
attempts.description: The correct 30 kOhm and 10 kOhm resistors are present, and a wire is drawn across the ideal source: the circuit does not compile.

expected.note: The two criteria that read the schematic are still evaluated.
